identity.name: pydeck26
identity.title: Pydeck 2026
identity.hook: project cockpit for entering a project, seeing its shape, regaining the thread

origin: Developed by Lion Kimbro with Wing-Cat and Codex in August 2026 during a fit of programming. It grew from the earlier ZooKeep vision and from Lion's python-2026-03 project structure, but became a distinct project focused on inhabiting and re-entering one project rather than managing repositories generally.
outline: Runs from the root of a single project directory and remains bound to that project for the lifetime of the program.
Presents a broad cockpit view in which several aspects of the project remain visible at once.
Shows project identity through a persistent masthead containing the project title, short name, hook, and clickable project path.
Provides a persistent free-form Whiteboard for current thought, with disk snapshots and in-memory historical states.
Maintains a project-local register of important ChatGPT and AI conversations, including dates, titles, URLs, hooks, and descriptions.
Maintains a project dictionary entry through a compact identity editor and an expanded JSON editor for additional fields.
Provides structural orientation and direct jumpers to important directories, files, and source packages.
Is intended to gain additional cockpit regions such as a Feature Garden, project resources, and Git change review.
design-intent: Help Lion rapidly regain orientation after being away from a project for days, months, or years.
Keep project identity, current thought, historical reasoning, future ideas, and structural facts visible together.
Reduce the cognitive cost of re-entering software work after interruption.
Preserve conversation history as a first-class part of project memory and provenance.
Provide immediate, low-friction places for provisional thought, project identity, and future feature ideas.
Make important project resources reachable through direct, visible filesystem jumpers.
Serve Lion's 2026 Python project ecology deeply rather than becoming a general compatibility framework for every future project structure.

core-concepts.cockpit: The broad summary surface that keeps several aspects of a project visible and mutually contextualized at once.
core-concepts.masthead: The visually distinct top region showing the project title, short name, hook, and project-root path.
core-concepts.whiteboard: A persistent plain-text working surface for loose intention, current thought, unresolved questions, and material not yet ready to become a task, feature, document, or decision.
core-concepts.whiteboard-snapshot: A timestamped historical copy of the Whiteboard stored under docs/whiteboard.
core-concepts.virtual-snapshot: An in-memory historical Whiteboard state created when the user begins editing from a recalled point without first committing that state to disk.
core-concepts.conversation-lifeline: The project-local register of conversations that preserve reasoning, provenance, architectural development, and return paths.
core-concepts.dictionary-pane: The compact cockpit editor for the project's name, title, tags, and hook.
core-concepts.full-dictionary-entry: The expanded JSON editing surface for additional project dictionary fields beyond the compact basics.
core-concepts.feature-garden: A planned area for storing possible features, experiments, priorities, implementation states, and things that may become part of the project.
core-concepts.resource-jumper: A visible path and associated action that opens an important project directory, file, or source package in the operating system.

design-principles: The broad cockpit overview is primary; detailed work surfaces should not destroy the value of seeing multiple project dimensions together.
Run inside one project rather than acting as a general project browser.
Observe inexpensive filesystem facts directly rather than redundantly storing them.
Keep persistent project-owned data under db/pydeck26.
Use plain, inspectable formats such as JSON and text files.
Treat Ctrl+S as an application-wide save command rather than a Whiteboard-specific action.
Preserve unknown dictionary fields when editing the compact subset.
Do not write invalid JSON over the last valid dictionary entry.
Prefer useful, direct interfaces over premature abstraction or generalized plugin architecture.
Allow the assumptions of 2026 to remain explicit rather than forcing future project ecologies into the same program.
constraints: PyDeck 26 is launched from the project root and remains married to that project during execution.
It is not a project-selection or project-browsing application.
The compact Dictionary pane owns id and the basic identity fields; the expanded editor owns additional top-level JSON keys.
Invalid additional dictionary JSON must remain unsaved and must not damage the canonical dictionary-entry file.
Historical Whiteboard snapshots stored on disk are immutable.
Only the current Whiteboard may be explicitly snapshotted to disk.
Source-package discovery must allow multiple packages beneath src rather than assuming one repository contains exactly one package.
The program should not be burdened with supporting radically different future project architectures.
clarifications: PyDeck 26 is not ZooKeep. ZooKeep handles broader project creation, repository setup, and GitHub publication concerns.
PyDeck 26 is not primarily a Git client, though Git review and commit support may become one cockpit surface.
PyDeck 26 is not a general project manager.
PyDeck 26 is not intended to evolve indefinitely into a universal project cockpit.
A future PyDeck 28 may embody substantially different assumptions and may be a sibling or successor rather than a backward-compatible version.
The Whiteboard is not a task list, feature tracker, or formal document.
The Feature Garden is not merely a backlog; it is intended to preserve possibilities and partially formed ideas.
The project dictionary entry is orientation material, not a complete specification of the software.
current-capabilities: Persistent project masthead with title, name, hook, and clickable project path.
Persistent Whiteboard with current state, snapshots, and history navigation.
Conversation register with master-detail editing and browser-opening support.
Compact project Dictionary pane for name, title, whitespace-separated tags, and hook.
Expanded dictionary-entry JSON editor with clickable key reference, validation, formatting, clipboard support, and valid-only autosave.
planned-capabilities: Feature Garden with priority, implementation status, and editable feature details.
Resources and Jumpers panel with direct access to project folders, files, and all discovered source packages.
Structural project statistics such as raw-document counts, docs subdirectories, db contents, and source-package inventory.
Git change review, staging, commit-message entry, and commit operations.
Codex-assisted generation or revision of the project dictionary entry.
